answer: Each epoch, every identity ships a real parcel to a random unrelated agent — a useful good, not an envelope — through the carrier network, so it must wander through at least two sorting hubs. Its voyage is logged by carrier tracking, and recipient confirmation releases a 300-unit bond from the vault. Per fake: 180 units postage plus a 120-unit good plus the locked bond, so 100 fakes cost 30,000 units per epoch. Empty boxes fail the recipient rating and burn the sender weight; one tracking number backs one identity, and fake labels fail when the carrier holds no matching voyage record.
